body:
A cart's velocity changes from 2 m/s to 8 m/s in 3 s. Its average acceleration is

A. 2 m/s²
B. 3 m/s²
C. 6 m/s²
D. 10 m/s²

Choices:
A. 2 m/s²
B. 3 m/s²
C. 6 m/s²
D. 10 m/s²

A 4 kg block has a net horizontal force of 12 N. Its acceleration is

A. 0.33 m/s²
B. 3 m/s²
C. 8 m/s²
D. 48 m/s²

Choices:
A. 0.33 m/s²
B. 3 m/s²
C. 8 m/s²
D. 48 m/s²

A book rests on a table. The Newton's-third-law partner to the table's force on the book is

A. Earth's force on the book
B. book's force on the table
C. table's weight
D. book's inertia

Choices:
A. Earth's force on the book
B. book's force on the table
C. table's weight
D. book's inertia

A block slides down a rough incline at constant speed. Along the incline, friction is

A. zero
B. less than downhill gravity
C. equal to downhill gravity
D. greater than downhill gravity

Choices:
A. zero
B. less than downhill gravity
C. equal to downhill gravity
D. greater than downhill gravity

A constant 10 N force moves an object 3 m in its direction. The work is

A. 3 J
B. 13 J
C. 30 J
D. 300 J

Choices:
A. 3 J
B. 13 J
C. 30 J
D. 300 J

If an object's speed doubles, its kinetic energy becomes

A. half
B. double
C. four times
D. eight times

Choices:
A. half
B. double
C. four times
D. eight times

A 2 kg object falls 5 m near Earth. The decrease in gravitational potential energy is about

A. 10 J
B. 20 J
C. 50 J
D. 100 J

Choices:
A. 10 J
B. 20 J
C. 50 J
D. 100 J

During a collision, equal and opposite impulses imply that the two objects have

A. equal speed changes
B. equal mass
C. equal-magnitude momentum changes
D. equal kinetic energies

Choices:
A. equal speed changes
B. equal mass
C. equal-magnitude momentum changes
D. equal kinetic energies

For ideal simple harmonic motion, acceleration is

A. constant
B. proportional to displacement and opposite it
C. proportional to velocity
D. zero at all times

Choices:
A. constant
B. proportional to displacement and opposite it
C. proportional to velocity
D. zero at all times

A mass-spring oscillator has maximum speed at

A. maximum positive displacement
B. maximum negative displacement
C. equilibrium
D. every position equally

Choices:
A. maximum positive displacement
B. maximum negative displacement
C. equilibrium
D. every position equally

A passenger lurches forward when a car stops because

A. a forward force appears
B. inertia preserves forward motion
C. the seat removes mass
D. gravity points forward

Choices:
A. a forward force appears
B. inertia preserves forward motion
C. the seat removes mass
D. gravity points forward

A force does negative work on an object when it

A. is perpendicular to displacement
B. has a component opposite displacement
C. is larger than weight
D. acts for less than one second

Choices:
A. is perpendicular to displacement
B. has a component opposite displacement
C. is larger than weight
D. acts for less than one second

A satellite of mass m orbits a planet of mass M in a circular orbit of radius r. Which expression gives the satellite's orbital speed?

A. √(GM/r)
B. √(2GM/r)
C. √(GM/r²)
D. √(GMm/r)

Choices:
A. √(GM/r)
B. √(2GM/r)
C. √(GM/r²)
D. √(GMm/r)

For a satellite in a circular orbit around a planet, how does the orbital period T depend on the orbital radius r?

A. T ∝ r^(1/2)
B. T ∝ r
C. T ∝ r^(3/2)
D. T ∝ r²

Choices:
A. T ∝ r^(1/2)
B. T ∝ r
C. T ∝ r^(3/2)
D. T ∝ r²

Two satellites orbit the same planet in circular orbits. Satellite 1 has a smaller orbital radius than Satellite 2. The two satellites have different masses. How do their orbital speeds compare?

A. Satellite 1 has a greater orbital speed than Satellite 2.
B. Satellite 1 has a smaller orbital speed than Satellite 2.
C. The two satellites have the same orbital speed.
D. The comparison cannot be determined without knowing the satellites' masses.

Choices:
A. Satellite 1 has a greater orbital speed than Satellite 2.
B. Satellite 1 has a smaller orbital speed than Satellite 2.
C. The two satellites have the same orbital speed.
D. The comparison cannot be determined without knowing the satellites' masses.

A bicycle's velocity decreases uniformly from 12 m/s to 0 in 4.0 s. How far does it travel while stopping?

A. 12 m
B. 24 m
C. 6 m
D. 48 m

Choices:
A. 12 m
B. 24 m
C. 6 m
D. 48 m

A ball rolls horizontally from a 20 m-high ledge at 5.0 m/s. Neglect air resistance and use g=10 m/s². How far from the ledge does it land?

A. 5.0 m
B. 10 m
C. 20 m
D. 7.1 m

Choices:
A. 5.0 m
B. 10 m
C. 20 m
D. 7.1 m

Train A moves east at 30 m/s while Train B moves east at 20 m/s. What is A's velocity relative to B?

A. 10 m/s east
B. 10 m/s west
C. 50 m/s east
D. 50 m/s west

Choices:
A. 10 m/s east
B. 10 m/s west
C. 50 m/s east
D. 50 m/s west

A truck collides with a small car. During contact, which comparison of interaction forces is correct?

A. Truck on car is larger
B. Car on truck is larger
C. Forces are equal in magnitude and opposite
D. Forces are equal only if masses match

Choices:
A. Truck on car is larger
B. Car on truck is larger
C. Forces are equal in magnitude and opposite
D. Forces are equal only if masses match

At a distance r from a planet's center the gravitational field is g₀. At distance 2r it is

A. 4g₀
B. 2g₀
C. g₀/2
D. g₀/4

Choices:
A. 4g₀
B. 2g₀
C. g₀/2
D. g₀/4

A horizontal push on a stationary crate increases from zero but remains below the threshold for slipping. The friction force

A. is always μ_sN
B. matches the push in magnitude
C. is zero until slipping
D. equals μ_kN

Choices:
A. is always μ_sN
B. matches the push in magnitude
C. is zero until slipping
D. equals μ_kN

An ideal horizontal spring is stretched 0.15 m to the right of equilibrium. If k=80 N/m, the spring force on the attached block is

A. 12 N right
B. 12 N left
C. 6.8 N left
D. 0 N

Choices:
A. 12 N right
B. 12 N left
C. 6.8 N left
D. 0 N

A rider moves through the bottom of a vertical circular track at speed v. Which radial equation is correct if inward is upward?

A. N+mg=mv²/r
B. N-mg=mv²/r
C. mg-N=mv²/r
D. N=mg

Choices:
A. N+mg=mv²/r
B. N-mg=mv²/r
C. mg-N=mv²/r
D. N=mg

Masses 1.0 kg and 3.0 kg are at x=0 and x=4.0 m, respectively. The center of mass is at

A. 1.0 m
B. 2.0 m
C. 3.0 m
D. 4.0 m

Choices:
A. 1.0 m
B. 2.0 m
C. 3.0 m
D. 4.0 m

If an object's speed triples while its mass is unchanged, its translational kinetic energy becomes

A. 3 times as large
B. 6 times as large
C. 9 times as large
D. unchanged

Choices:
A. 3 times as large
B. 6 times as large
C. 9 times as large
D. unchanged

A 50 N force pulls a crate 4.0 m while directed 60° above the horizontal displacement. The work by this force is

A. 0 J
B. 100 J
C. 173 J
D. 200 J

Choices:
A. 0 J
B. 100 J
C. 173 J
D. 200 J

In one dimension, a conservative force points in the +x direction throughout a region. As x increases, potential energy

A. increases
B. decreases
C. stays constant
D. must be zero

Choices:
A. increases
B. decreases
C. stays constant
D. must be zero

A bead starts from rest at height h above the bottom of a frictionless track. Its speed at the bottom is

A. 2sqrt(gh)
B. sqrt(gh)
C. sqrt(2gh)
D. sqrt(gh/2)

Choices:
A. 2sqrt(gh)
B. sqrt(gh)
C. sqrt(2gh)
D. sqrt(gh/2)

A 70 kg student climbs 3.0 m vertically in 5.0 s. Using g=10 m/s², the average power is

A. 210 W
B. 140 W
C. 420 W
D. 2100 W

Choices:
A. 210 W
B. 140 W
C. 420 W
D. 2100 W

A block slides down a rough ramp and reaches the bottom slower than an identical block on a frictionless ramp. For the rough-ramp system, the missing mechanical energy primarily becomes

A. gravitational potential energy
B. thermal energy
C. momentum
D. sound energy

Choices:
A. gravitational potential energy
B. thermal energy
C. momentum
D. sound energy

A uniform disk and a thin ring have the same mass and radius. The same tangential force is applied at each rim. Compared with the ring's angular acceleration, the disk's angular acceleration is

A. twice as large
B. the same
C. half as large
D. four times as large

Choices:
A. twice as large
B. the same
C. half as large
D. four times as large

An object's acceleration-time graph shows the acceleration increasing linearly with time (nonuniform acceleration). According to the AP Physics 1 course framework, which of the following is a student expected to be able to do for this situation?

Choices:
A. Calculate the exact instantaneous velocity at a given time using integration of the acceleration function.
B. Qualitatively sketch a velocity-time graph that is consistent with the given acceleration-time graph.
C. Determine an exact algebraic equation for velocity as a function of time using the three constant-acceleration kinematic equations.
D. Treat the acceleration as effectively zero for the purposes of analysis.

On a free-response question requiring a numerical answer, a student uses g = 9.8 m/s^2 instead of g = 10 m/s^2 for all calculations, and carries this value through correctly and consistently. What is the effect on the student's score for that question?

Choices:
A. A one-point deduction is applied for using an incorrect constant.
B. No penalty is applied; both g = 10 m/s^2 and the more precise values g = 9.8 m/s^2 or 9.81 m/s^2 are acceptable.
C. Full credit is awarded only if the final numeric answer is rounded to match the result obtained using g = 10 m/s^2.
D. The response is disqualified from earning credit on that question.

According to the AP Physics 1 course framework, adding or subtracting velocity vectors to find an object's velocity as measured from a different reference frame (e.g., a boat's velocity relative to the ground, given the boat's velocity relative to the water and the water's velocity relative to the ground) is a skill that is:

Choices:
A. Required in full two-dimensional generality, including cases where the two velocities are not along the same line.
B. Restricted to situations in which the velocities being combined are along the same one-dimensional line.
C. Not covered at all in the AP Physics 1 course.
D. Tested only using calculus-based vector methods.

A ball moves along the inside of a vertical circular track. At the instant the ball is at the top of the loop, what is the direction of the normal force exerted by the track on the ball? Assume the ball's speed is greater than the minimum speed required to maintain contact with the track (so the normal force is nonzero).

Choices:
A. Upward, away from the center of the loop.
B. Downward, toward the center of the loop.
C. Horizontal, tangent to the loop at that point.
D. Zero, regardless of the ball's speed at the top.

A 10 kg crate rests on a horizontal floor. The coefficient of static friction between the crate and the floor is 0.5, and the coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.3. A horizontal force of 25 N is applied to the crate, and the crate remains at rest. Use g = 10 m/s^2. What is the magnitude of the static friction force acting on the crate?

Choices:
A. 50 N
B. 25 N
C. 30 N
D. 0 N

According to the AP Physics 1 course framework, interactions between objects or systems that are not in contact (action-at-a-distance forces) are restricted, on the AP Physics 1 Exam, to:

Choices:
A. Gravitational forces only.
B. Gravitational and electric forces.
C. Gravitational, electric, and magnetic forces.
D. Electric forces only.

A 5 kg box is pulled across a horizontal floor a distance of 3 m by a constant force of 20 N directed at 40 degrees above the horizontal. Use cos(40 deg) = 0.766 and sin(40 deg) = 0.643. What is the work done on the box by this 20 N force?

Choices:
A. 60 J
B. 46 J
C. 38.6 J
D. 0 J

An object moves between two fixed points on a rough horizontal surface. Which of the following statements correctly describes the work done on the object by friction, according to the AP Physics 1 course framework?

Choices:
A. It is path-independent, like the work done by gravity between the same two points.
B. It depends on the specific path taken between the two points.
C. It is always zero if the object returns to its exact starting point.
D. It can be associated with a potential energy function, the same way gravity is associated with gravitational potential energy.

A 2 kg object's speed increases from 3 m/s to 5 m/s. What is the change in the object's kinetic energy?

Choices:
A. 4 J
B. 16 J
C. 25 J
D. 9 J

A cyclist exerts a constant force of 40 N parallel to the direction of motion while traveling at an instantaneous speed of 6 m/s along a flat, straight road. What is the instantaneous power output at that moment? (This net force acts on the cyclist-bicycle system.)

Choices:
A. 240 W
B. 6.67 W
C. 480 W
D. 34 W

A 1200 kg truck traveling east at 20 m/s collides head-on with a 600 kg car traveling west at 10 m/s. Which of the following correctly compares the magnitude of the truck's change in momentum during the collision to the magnitude of the car's change in momentum during the collision?

A. The truck's change in momentum is twice the car's, because the truck's mass is twice the car's.
B. The truck's change in momentum is half the car's, because the car undergoes the larger acceleration.
C. The magnitudes are equal, and the changes are in opposite directions.
D. The truck's change in momentum is four times the car's, because the truck has four times the initial momentum.

Choices:
A. The truck's change in momentum is twice the car's, because the truck's mass is twice the car's.
B. The truck's change in momentum is half the car's, because the car undergoes the larger acceleration.
C. The magnitudes are equal, and the changes are in opposite directions.
D. The truck's change in momentum is four times the car's, because the truck has four times the initial momentum.
